counterfactual.change: Changed bodies[0].e from 1 to 0 (single field). Inelastic bounce dissipates energy and avoids the erroneous energy injection, so same wall impact no longer violates energy_bound.

explanation: Shrunk to 1 body (e=1, m=1, r=0.833, vx=43.86) with no walls (arena boundary only). Energy is conserved until the high-speed impact with the right arena wall between step 137 and 138. Speed jumps from 43.89 to 49.07 (vx magnitude 43.86 -> 49.04) despite e=1 which should be elastic (conserve kinetic energy), increasing total mechanical energy from ~1054 J to 1294.6 J, exceeding E0*1.10+5=1164.4 J. Likely cause is the wall collision/positional-correction logic adding energy when correcting penetration at high incident velocity with split substeps (2 substeps in step 138), effectively injecting kinetic energy instead of reflecting it.
vision_note: From steps 135 to 137 the single blue body remains pinned against the right arena wall near the top with almost no frame-to-frame displacement. At step 138 it abruptly pops a short distance inward/downward away from the wall instead of executing a clean elastic reflection, indicating a high-speed wall impact with faulty correction.
